### Why S5 did not beat the previous stage

`v0` is pinned at its lower bound, meaning the optimiser wants an even longer arrival delay than the physical celerity range allows. That is what it does when the data contains **no propagation structure to find**: the best available fit is to push the shifted kernel as far out of the way as possible. Check the discharge source before blaming the model. The synthetic stand-in generates each reach's hydrograph independently — a per-reach annual factor and its own linear reservoir — so **there is no wave travelling between reaches in it at all**. A travel-time shift fitted against data with no travel time in it can only hurt, and this comparison becomes informative only once `data_mode.glofas` is `real`.

Doc 07 §11 plans for exactly this: *"Falling back to S3 with an honest explanation still leaves you with a working multitype spatio-temporal Hawkes model for Kerala hazards, which nobody has published. Do not treat S5 as all-or-nothing."*

**S5 — celerity check** (Doc 07 §10 gate 7): v0 = 4.00 gives median celerity 0.86 m/s (5-95th 0.25-2.46); OUTSIDE the physical range 1.0-5.0 m/s

**S5 — runout gate** (Doc 07 §10 gate 6): Mundakkai crown: d_slope 684 m vs fitted runout reach 2768 m (c = 2768 m, gamma = 0.446) — PASSES

## Stability, and why alpha is bounded by the network

Doc 07 §7 rule 7 makes a branching ratio at or above 1 an automatic invalid fit, whatever the likelihood says. The excitation parameters are therefore bounded **by the size of the set each source can reach**.

`alpha_LF` is not a count of offspring — it is the excitation applied to *each* reach downstream, and a landslide in this basin reaches a few hundred of them. So the quantity that must stay below 1 is `alpha_LF × (mean downstream set size)`, and the bound on `alpha_LF` scales down accordingly. Bounding `alpha_LF` itself at some fixed number would be far too generous the moment the network switches on at S4 — which is exactly how the first S4 fit came back at **1.569** and was rejected as explosive.

A branching ratio sitting exactly at its bound means the data wants more self-excitation than stationarity permits. That is reported, not fixed by raising the bound.

Every fit writes a JSON record to `models/fits/` carrying parameters, intervals, log-likelihood, AIC, seed, git commit and wall-clock time, so every number here traces back to a specific run (Doc 07 §7 rule 8).
